2026-05-13.title: Rep 1: Working Memory
2026-05-13.instruction: We'll show 7 items for 8 seconds. Memorize the order.
2026-05-13.prompt: Tokyo · Lisbon · Cairo · Oslo · Lima · Vienna · Seoul
2026-05-13.question: Which city was at position 5?
2026-05-13.explanation: Healthy working memory holds 7 ± 2 items for 15-30 seconds without rehearsal. The trick most people use unconsciously is chunking — grouping items by region (Tokyo–Seoul = East Asia, Lisbon–Vienna = Europe, Cairo = Africa, Lima = South America). When you chunk, you remember fewer slots.

2026-05-13.title: Rep 2: Source Evaluation
2026-05-13.instruction: A claim is presented with four possible sources. Pick the most credible one.
2026-05-13.prompt: Claim: Adults who consume two or more cups of green tea daily show approximately 18% lower risk of stroke compared to non-consumers, after controlling for diet and exercise.
2026-05-13.question: Which source most credibly supports this claim?
choices: A 2024 meta-analysis in Stroke journal pooling 14 cohort studies (n=550,000) across multiple countries
A viral Twitter thread by a self-described 'longevity researcher' with 800K followers
A press release from the Global Tea Industry Association announcing new product benefits
A Healthline aggregator article titled '11 Reasons Green Tea Is a Superfood'
2026-05-13.explanation: A meta-analysis in a specialty peer-reviewed journal aggregating hundreds of thousands of subjects across countries is the gold standard. The other three are: anecdote/personal authority, industry-funded press release with conflict of interest, and content-marketing aggregator. Source evaluation is the muscle most easily atrophied by AI summaries that blend source types without weighting.

2026-05-13.title: Rep 3: Inference
2026-05-13.instruction: Given the premises, identify the valid conclusion.
2026-05-13.prompt:
Premise 1: All members of the international research consortium who completed peer review training before 2024 received the senior reviewer designation.
Premise 2: Dr. Mendez did not receive the senior reviewer designation.
Premise 3: Receiving the senior reviewer designation requires completing peer review training before 2024.
2026-05-13.question: Which conclusion is logically VALID?
choices: Dr. Mendez did not complete peer review training before 2024
Dr. Mendez completed peer review training after 2024
Dr. Mendez was exempt from the training requirement
2026-05-13.explanation: From Premise 3 (Senior → CompletedBefore2024) and Premise 2 (¬Senior), modus tollens gives ¬CompletedBefore2024. Option C is wrong: 'didn't complete before 2024' doesn't mean 'completed after 2024' — Mendez might have never completed it. Conflating absence-of-evidence with evidence-of-absence is one of the most common reasoning errors.

2026-05-13.title: Rep 4: Pattern Recognition
2026-05-13.instruction: Identify the next number in the sequence.
2026-05-13.question: What's the next number?
2026-05-13.explanation: Differences between terms: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, **14**. So 42 + 14 = 56. The closed form is n(n+1): 1·2=2, 2·3=6, 3·4=12... 7·8=56. Pattern recognition is the cognitive skill most easily outsourced to AI ('what's the pattern?'), so it's the most at risk of atrophy.

2026-05-13.title: Rep 5: Estimation
2026-05-13.instruction: A Fermi-style estimation problem. Take your time — no timer.
2026-05-13.prompt: Approximately how many cups of espresso are pulled across all bars and cafés in central Rome (the historic core, not the entire metropolitan area) on a typical weekday?
2026-05-13.question: Your best estimate:
2026-05-13.explanation: Decompose: central Rome has roughly 1,500-2,500 bars and cafés serving espresso. Italians average 2-3 espressos per day; tourists in Rome consume similar amounts. With ~600K daytime population including commuters and tourists, total espresso events are 1.2M-1.8M city-wide. Central Rome captures perhaps 25-30% of this concentration. Fermi estimation — decompose, multiply, sanity-check — is the antidote to 'just ask AI for a number you can't verify.'
